reasoning: Three acts, read to the end of the turn. First, a request for a plain-text session plan in this window, 5-10 lines with emoticon statuses: asking for a plan or status is asking for something to be made, so it is work like any other, and its scope to this session means it states no standing rule. Second, questions about the worker: is it doing the whole plan or only part, and what comes out at the end. Those are answered, not turned into tickets, and answering them may take reading, which is not work. Third, a reported fact that everything was copied to the worker and it was launched, kept as evidence; a fact reported alongside a request is still its own act and does not dissolve into the request. One new result is accepted, so the ticket is admitted and taken in hand in the same call. Nothing already in flight has its goal changed, so nothing attaches. The accepted work only produces a written status list for a person, so it touches documentation and communication alone, and needs no specialist: routing a plain request for a plan to the communicator is how the request disappears.
